activities.title: Student Profile and Study-Time Card guided Build

contract.doing: Create `student-profile/profile_card.py` from the supplied starter. Ask for a name and planned weekly study minutes, convert the minutes to an integer, calculate hours and remaining minutes, and print a labelled profile card with f-strings. Then deliberately reproduce and repair one NameError and one indentation or missing-colon failure.
contract.why: This first program establishes the habits every later practical requires: save the intended file, run the exact command, inspect values, and use a traceback rather than guessing.
contract.output: A `student-profile` folder containing a runnable `profile_card.py` and `evidence.md` with three successful cases and two evidence-led repairs.
contract.tools: Windows, stable Python 3, VS Code, and PowerShell
contract.prerequisites: Only verified setup capabilities and this Week’s Core Study are required.
contract.finished: The same saved file runs from PowerShell with the documented command. The program converts minutes and reports correct hour/remainder values for 360, 95, and 0. Output uses labelled f-strings and the learner can identify string versus integer values. Evidence records distinct NameError and syntax/indentation failures and the clue used to repair each.
contract.submission: Exact folder path, Python run command, and final source filename | Three-case expected-versus-actual table | NameError traceback clue and repaired line | Syntax or indentation clue and final clean rerun

steps: Create the folder and file, paste the starter exactly, save it, run `py profile_card.py`, and record the initial output before adding input.
Add the supplied name and minutes prompts. Convert minutes with `int`, calculate `hours = minutes // 60` and `remaining_minutes = minutes % 60`, and print a four-line card with f-strings.
Run three cases: 360 minutes, 95 minutes, and 0 minutes. Record the input, predicted card, and actual card before changing any code.
Change one use of `name` to `student_name` without changing the assignment. Run the unchanged command, record the last traceback line and highlighted name, then repair it.
Use the supplied tiny if block to reproduce one missing-colon or indentation error. Record the exception type and caret/line clue, repair it, then rerun all three cases.
Create `evidence.md` with the exact command, three-case table, two broken lines, traceback clues, repairs, and final clean output.

Evidence records distinct NameError and syntax/indentation failures and the clue used to repair each.

activities.title: Course Registration Eligibility Checker guided Build

contract.doing: Create `registration-checker/check_registration.py`. Ask for age, entrance score, and whether the prerequisite course is complete. Convert the two numeric fields narrowly, normalize the yes/no value, and apply the supplied ordered contract: valid ages are 16–120, scores are 0–100, a score of at least 50 and completed prerequisite are required.
contract.why: Practical exams frequently combine conversion, comparisons, Boolean logic, and ordered branches. A registration decision makes boundary values and invalid text visible without hiding errors.
contract.output: A registration checker with a stable rule order, seven-case record, narrow ValueError handling, and one documented Boolean repair.
contract.tools: Windows, stable Python 3, VS Code, and PowerShell
contract.prerequisites: Previously completed competencies: PYIN-C001, PYIN-C002, PYIN-C003. New Week concepts are taught in Core Study before this Build.
contract.finished: Numeric conversion catches ValueError without a broad catch-all. The supplied age and score ranges include their boundary values. Only normalized yes or no values are accepted for the prerequisite. All seven cases produce exactly one documented message, and the Boolean-operator defect is repaired.
contract.submission: Source path and exact run command | Seven-case expected-versus-actual table | ValueError result for nonnumeric input | Incorrect and repaired Boolean condition with the same rerun case

steps: Copy the supplied decision contract into `README.md` and predict all seven cases before coding.
Collect the three inputs and use one small try block for `int(age_text)` and `int(score_text)`. On ValueError, print `INVALID: age and score must be whole numbers.` and do not evaluate eligibility.
Normalize the prerequisite answer with `strip().lower()` and accept only yes or no. Then order the remaining checks: yes/no validity, numeric ranges, missing prerequisite, score below 50, success.
Run the seven supplied cases and record exactly one output per case. Confirm age 16, score 50 is accepted when the prerequisite is yes.
Deliberately replace one `and` with `or` in the success condition. Record the misclassified case, restore the operator, and rerun the same case.
Keep the source, README contract, case table, and defect note together in the project folder.

Only normalized yes or no values are accepted for the prerequisite.
All seven cases produce exactly one documented message, and the Boolean-operator defect is repaired.
